sources.title: Suno Studio 2.0 — official help documentation

limitations: Product documentation is capability evidence, not independent benchmark performance.

sources.title: Google Lyria RealTime API documentation
sources.scope: Persistent streaming audio generation with live prompt and configuration steering.

limitations: Streaming audio controls are not equivalent to symbolic note/event editing.

sources.title: YuE2: Agentic Score Planning and Editing for Music Generation
sources.scope: Score-first full-song planning and realization, with conversational score/arrangement editing described in the research release.
limitations: Research capability description is not a matched independent preference result.

sources.title: MAGE: Modality-Agnostic Music Generation and Mixture-Grounded Editing
sources.scope: Multimodal conditional music generation and mixture-grounded target-source editing.
limitations: Generation/source-extraction comparison, not general symbolic score-edit correctness.

sources.title: JAM_BOT: Expressive Human–AI Musical Improvisation
sources.scope: Real-time symbolic and expressive human–AI improvisation, with variable-tempo call-and-response and MIDI timing work.
limitations: Closest live symbolic-interaction comparator, but not a matched result against Muse yet.
Performance depends on instrument, clock, MIDI interface, buffering and latency compensation.

sources.title: TimingBench: Are you rushing or dragging? A benchmark for temporal controllability in text-to-music generation
sources.scope: 250 prompts for 30-second instrumental clips: 100 single-event, 100 timed-sequence, 50 global-tempo prompts; 399 timestamped events and 50 tempo targets across about 40 style descriptors and nine instrument families.
limitations: The public result is published by Taan, one of the evaluated systems; independent replication is not established by this snapshot.
Its 128-event detector validation sample is development data and reports 4 false credits and 6 false positives.
A separate planned 300-clip annotation study was unfinished at the reported evaluation cutoff.
Detector localization floors vary substantially by event family; a single timing tolerance must not be interpreted as equally precise for drums, bass, vocals, and whole-mix events.
The benchmark uses a ±500 ms timed-event criterion; this is not equivalent to MIDI beat-phase precision, sub-100-ms timing, or live system latency.
FAD measures distribution similarity under a fixed VGGish/GTZAN procedure, not listener preference or reciprocal collaboration.

sources.title: CMI-RewardBench: Evaluating Music Reward Models with Compositional Multimodal Instruction — official results and toolkit
sources.published_or_observed_at: ICML 2026; official repository snapshot observed 21 November 2026
sources.scope: Reward-model evaluation for generated music conditioned on text, lyrics and reference audio. Public result tables report musicality correlations/accuracy and compositional alignment accuracy for CMI-RM, SongEval-RM, Gemini 3 Pro and CLAP.
sources.version_snapshot: CMI-RewardBench ICML 2026 official release repository snapshot
limitations: This evaluates reward models/judges, not music generators; scores are not generation quality or a direct comparison to audio Elo.
The 110k CMIPref-Pseudo items are pseudo-labelled, not 110k human preference labels.
The CMI-Pref corpus is human annotated; the author and institutional materials report roughly 4,027 human preference labels, but do not assume that is the sample size for every displayed metric.
The README gives selected competitive metrics; use the paper and official evaluation script for full reproduction, split definitions, confidence intervals and subgroup analysis.
Reward-model outputs can be biased or miscalibrated and must not authorize edits or substitute for artist preference.

sources.title: MIREX 2026 Music Evaluation via CMI-RewardBench — results
sources.scope: Pairwise preference prediction for text prompts and generated audio pairs. Public table reports a 249-sample core set plus vocal and instrumental extension subsets of 300+ samples each.
limitations: This measures agreement with pairwise human preference labels, not generation quality, edit fidelity, musician agency, or live collaboration.
The core test set contains 249 comparisons; subgroup extensions are shown as 300+ rather than exact counts on the results table.
A row labelled Random guess (always B) obtains 59.0% on the core set, demonstrating label imbalance; this is not a balanced 50% random-choice baseline.
Submission labels and score tables do not alone establish open weights, code availability, evaluation-cost parity or independent replication.
Do not treat these preference accuracies as CMI-RM's native correlation metrics or as audio-generation Elo.

sources.title: LLMs can read music, but struggle to hear it: an evaluation of core music perception tasks
sources.scope: MUSE music-perception study contrasts audio and symbolic-MIDI inputs for syncopation scoring, melody transposition detection and chord-quality identification, across Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash and Qwen2.5-Omni; also compares zero/few-shot and Standalone/CoT/LogicLM prompting.
limitations: Published figures report model/task/modality-specific accuracy; several values entered in this ledger are approximate visual estimates from Figure 2, not exact Table 1 raw counts.
The reported perceptual gap is model- and task-dependent: Gemini Pro approaches parity on transposition, but audio performance remains much weaker for syncopation and chord quality.
The study uses short, controlled excerpts; it is not a benchmark of full-length composition, free-form improvisation or commercial music production.
MIDI accuracy is symbolic-input performance and must never be reported as audio-native listening competence.

comparison_rules: Only compare scores within the same benchmark, version, split, modality, task definition and metric implementation.
Never compare instrumental Elo, vocal Elo, symbolic 0–5 ratings, editing accuracy or reciprocal-interaction effects as if they shared a scale.
Reproduce the external baseline on its official split before tuning or claiming improvement.
Pin exact model/API version, date, prompt set, decoding, retries, compute budget, renderer and scorer digest for every new result.
Retain every attempt, parse failure, timeout, abstention and invalid output in the denominator or report it explicitly.
A product feature list is not benchmark performance; a benchmark score is not proof of agency, authorship, rights or collaboration.
Use matched capability surfaces. For audio-only APIs, do not fabricate note-level or score-level controls.
Publish quality, exact editing, preservation, latency, recovery, agency, rights/provenance and cost as separate dimensions; do not collapse them into a composite score.
All numerical targets for Muse are prospective qualification objectives until a pinned, exact-head result and independent evaluation evidence exist.
